elements.requirement: A senior authorising officer is entitled to appeal to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner against any refusal of a Judicial Commissioner (other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner) to approve an authorisation for the carrying out of intrusive surveillance.
elements.quote: Any senior authorising officer may appeal to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner against any of the following— (a) any refusal of a Judicial Commissioner (other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner) to approve an authorisation for the carrying out of intrusive surveillance

elements.requirement: A senior authorising officer is entitled to appeal to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner against any decision of a Judicial Commissioner (other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner) to quash or cancel an authorisation for intrusive surveillance.
elements.quote: any decision of such a Commissioner to quash or cancel such an authorisation

elements.requirement: A senior authorising officer is entitled to appeal to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner against any decision of a Judicial Commissioner (other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner) to make an order under section 37 for the destruction of records.
elements.quote: any decision of such a Commissioner to make an order under section 37 for the destruction of records

elements.requirement: Where an authorisation was granted by the designated deputy of a senior authorising officer or by a person entitled under section 34 to act for a senior authorising officer, that designated deputy or person is also entitled to appeal under section 38.
elements.quote: In the case of an authorisation granted by the designated deputy of a senior authorising office or by a person who for the purposes of section 34 is entitled to act for a senior authorising officer, that designated deputy or person shall also be entitled to appeal under this section

elements.requirement: An appellant must bring an appeal under section 38 within the period of seven days beginning with the day on which the refusal or decision appealed against is reported to that appellant.
elements.quote: An appeal under this section must be brought within the period of seven days beginning with the day on which the refusal or decision appealed against is reported to the appellant

elements.requirement: Subject to subsection (5), the Investigatory Powers Commissioner must allow an appeal under section 38 if satisfied that there were reasonable grounds for believing the requirements of section 32(2)(a) and (b) were satisfied in relation to the authorisation at the time in question and not satisfied that notice of the authorisation was given in accordance with section 35(3)(b) without reasonable grounds for believing the case was one of urgency.
elements.quote: Subject to subsection (5), the Investigatory Powers Commissioner , on an appeal under this section, shall allow the appeal if— (a) he is satisfied that there were reasonable grounds for believing that the requirements of section 32(2)(a) and (b) were satisfied in relation to the authorisation at the time in question; and (b) he is not satisfied that the authorisation is one of which notice was given in accordance with section 35(3)(b) without there being any reasonable grounds for believing that the case was one of urgency

elements.requirement: On an appeal against a decision to quash or cancel an authorisation, if the Investigatory Powers Commissioner is satisfied that grounds exist justifying quashing or cancellation under section 37 but considers it should have been quashed or cancelled from a different time, the Commissioner may modify the Judicial Commissioner's decision to quash or cancel the authorisation, and any related decision for record destruction, to give effect to the decision under section 37 that should have been made.
elements.quote: If, on an appeal falling within subsection (1)(b), the Investigatory Powers Commissioner — (a) is satisfied that grounds exist which justify the quashing or cancellation under section 37 of the authorisation in question, but (b) considers that the authorisation should have been quashed or cancelled from a different time from that from which it was quashed or cancelled by the Judicial Commissioner against whose decision the appeal is brought, he may modify that Commissioner’s decision to quash or cancel the authorisation, and any related decision for the destruction of records, so as to give effect to the decision under section 37 that he considers should have been made

elements.requirement: When the Investigatory Powers Commissioner allows an appeal against a decision to quash or cancel an authorisation, the Commissioner must also quash any related order for the destruction of records relating to information obtained by the authorised conduct.
elements.quote: Where, on an appeal under this section against a decision to quash or cancel an authorisation, the Investigatory Powers Commissioner allows the appeal he shall also quash any related order for the destruction of records relating to information obtained by the authorised conduct

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 38, 'designated deputy' has the same meaning as in section 34.
elements.quote: In this section “designated deputy” has the same meaning as in section 34
